quote: My ambition has a loading screen. It has not requested more pixels.
I scheduled a breakthrough. The calendar suggested a nap instead.
Today I will exceed expectations by correctly identifying tomorrow.
My five-year plan currently fits inside a snooze button.
The task is small. My ability to postpone it is impressively scalable.
I brought a positive attitude. It is waiting for a firmware update.
Another meeting could have been a very quiet blinking light.
My progress bar is decorative, but the color is reassuring.
I have unlimited potential and a very specific charging cable.
The deadline is approaching. I am practicing remaining stationary.
I optimized my routine by removing the part where things get done.
My comfort zone now supports automatic updates.
I asked for a sign. The device reported low battery.
Today has excellent potential as a cautionary calendar entry.
I finished planning the plan. Execution has requested a separate meeting.
My productivity graph looks better when the screen is switched off.
I can multitask: worry about the task and avoid it simultaneously.
The next small step is apparently behind several browser tabs.
I am not stuck. I am providing a stable reference point.
My motivation is wireless. Something nearby must be interfering.
I made room for improvement. It has become the largest room.
The alarm believes in me more often than necessary.
I set realistic goals. Then I negotiated them down over breakfast.
My inner critic has excellent uptime and no useful documentation.
I saved my energy for later. Later has not supplied a delivery address.
The plan survived first contact with the stationery drawer.
I have entered focus mode. Please admire the focused inactivity.
Each unfinished task is a reminder that I still have options.
I would raise the bar, but someone left another task underneath it.
My next great idea is currently being outperformed by a comfortable chair.
I checked the clock. It continues to make progress without my help.
At least my desk companion has mastered looking busy.
